rows.question: What did the king do after he had the hat, cloak and boots?
answers: wished himself far away
He wished himself far away
rows.said: He wished himself far away.

rows.question: Why did the king pretend to help decide the brothers quarrel?
answers: to trick them
To wish himself back to whiteland
rows.said: To test the brothers' possessions and decide their quarrel.

rows.question: What did the North Wind offer to do when the king stands on the steps beside the door?
answers: come roaring up as though he were going to tear down the whole castle
The North Wind took him and carried him off
rows.said: The North Wind would take the prince along with him.

rows.question: Why did the queen not recognize the king at first?
answers: He had grown thin and pale.
He had grown thin and pale
rows.said: She was very sad and had wished herself home.

rows.question: What made the queen recognize the king?
answers: He showed her the ring.
The ring
rows.said: The ring with the power of granting two wishes.

rows.question: Where did the poor young widow woman live?
answers: in a house called Kittlerumpit
Kittlerumpit
rows.said: In a house called Kittlerumpit.

rows.question: Why did people pity the widowed Mistress of Kittlerumpit?
answers: She had lost her husband, and no one quite knew what had become of him.
She had lost her husband
rows.said: Because she had lost her husband and no one knew what had become of him.

rows.question: What did some people say about her husband?
answers: had been persuaded to enlist, and had been killed in the wars
Killed in the wars
rows.said: Some people said he had been persuaded to enlist and killed in war, while others claimed he was taken by the press-gang and drowned at sea.

rows.question: What did others say about her husband?
answers: had been taken away to serve as a sailor by the press-gang, and had been drowned at sea
Taken away to serve as a sailor
rows.said: Others said he had been killed in war or taken as a sailor by the press-gang.

rows.question: Who was the widowed Mistress of Kittlerumpit left with?
answers: a little baby-boy
A little baby-boy
rows.said: A little baby-boy.

rows.question: Why didn't the widowed Mistress of Kittlerumpit have much to live on?
answers: Times were bad.
Times were bad
rows.said: She had lost her husband and was left with a baby to raise.

rows.question: What did the widowed Mistress do to earn enough money?
answers: worked all day amongst her cows, and pigs, and hens
Worked all day amongst her cows, and pigs and hens
rows.said: She worked all day among her cows, pigs, and hens to earn money.

rows.question: Why did the widowed Mistress rise very early and go out to feed her pigs?
answers: Rent-day was coming on, and she intended to take one of them, a great, big, fat creature, to the market that very day.
Rent-day was coming on
rows.said: To earn money for rent and food.

rows.question: Why did the widowed Mistress want to sell her pig?
answers: She thought that the price that it would fetch would go a long way towards paying her rent.
The price it would fetch would go a long way towards paying her rent
rows.said: To pay her rent.

rows.question: How did the widowed Mistress feel while she thought of selling the pig?
answers: happy
Very happy
rows.said: She felt light-hearted and happy.

rows.question: How did the widowed Mistress feel after she saw her dying pig?
answers: sad
Despair
rows.said: She felt despair.

rows.question: What happened after the widowed Mistress reached the pig stye?
answers: Her pig looked as if it was going to die.
There lay her cherish pig on its back
rows.said: She cried out in despair over her lost pig.

rows.question: Why did the widowed Mistress feel upset after she saw her cherished pig on its back?
answers: She was going to lose her finest pig.
It was going to breathe its last breath
rows.said: She felt upset because she had lost her husband and now had to lose her only source of income.

rows.question: Who looked like a lady born?
answers: an Old Woman
Old Woman
rows.said: The Old Woman.

rows.question: What did the widowed Mistress do as the Old Woman drew near?
answers: rise and curtsey to the Gentlewoman
Curtsey
rows.said: She felt it was becoming to rise and curtsey to the Gentlewoman.

rows.question: Why was the widowed Mistress the most unfortunate woman in the world?
answers: She lost her husband and her pig.
Lost her husband
rows.said: She had lost her husband and was left with a baby to raise while her pig was dying.

rows.question: What did the widowed Mistress need to do before the Old Woman could help her cure the pig?
answers: offer something in return
Give her something in return for curing the pig
rows.said: She had to promise to pay the Old Woman's price for curing the pig.

rows.question: How will the widowed Mistress feel after the Old Woman offers to cure her pig?
answers: delighted
Delighted
rows.said: She will feel delighted and relieved.

rows.question: Why did the widowed Mistress make a rash promise?
answers: She was too happy that her pig was going to be saved.
The old woman could ask for anything in return
rows.said: She was too delighted to think she was making a rash promise.

rows.question: What did the Old Woman do after the widowed Mistress made a promise to her?
answers: walked straight into the pig-sty
Walked straight into the pig-sty
rows.said: She walked straight into the pig-sty.

rows.question: What did the Old Woman do while she looked at the dying creature?
answers: rocked to and fro and muttering to herself
Mutter to herself
rows.said: She rocked to and fro and mumbled to herself.

rows.question: What did the Old Woman take out of her pocket?
answers: a tiny bottle
A tiny bottle
rows.said: A tiny bottle with a liquid that looked like oil.

rows.question: What happened after the Old Woman touched the pig on the snout, ears, and tail?
answers: The pig was cured.
The beast jumped
rows.said: The pig jumped up and ran to its trough to eat.

rows.question: How will the widowed Mistress feel after the Old Woman cures her pig?
answers: joyful
Relieved
rows.said: She will feel relief and gratitude.

rows.question: Why did the widowed Mistress feel joyful after the Old Woman cured her pig?
answers: She felt that her rent was safe.
She felt that her rent was safe
rows.said: She felt joyful because she believed the Old Woman had saved her pig's life, which would secure her rent payment.

rows.question: What did the widowed Mistress want to do to show her gratitude?
answers: kiss the hem of the strange Lady's green gown
She would have kissed the hem of the strange Lady's green gown
rows.said: She intended to kiss the hem of the Fairy's gown.

rows.question: Why didn't the Old Woman allow the widowed Mistress to kiss the hem of her gown?
answers: They needed to focus on their bargain.
She wanted to stick to the bargain
rows.said: Because the Old Woman was a wicked Fairy who demanded the widow's son in exchange for saving her pig.

rows.question: What did the Old Woman ask for in return?
answers: her son
The son
rows.said: The Old Woman asked for the widow's son.

rows.question: How did the widowed Mistress feel after she needed to give her son to the Old Woman?
answers: sad
Very sad
rows.said: She felt despair and regret.

rows.question: Why did the poor widow give a piteous cry?
answers: The Old Woman was a wicked fairy.
The Green-clad Lady was a fairy
rows.said: She realized the Green-clad Lady was a wicked Fairy who demanded her son as payment for saving her pig.

rows.question: What did the widowed Mistress do after the Old Woman demanded to take her son?
answers: prayed, and beseeched, and begged for mercy
Gave a piteous cry
rows.said: She cried out that she knew the Green-clad Lady was a wicked Fairy and refused to give her son.

rows.question: What did the widowed Mistress need to do to keep her son?
answers: find out the Old Woman's name
Find out the fairy's name
rows.said: She promised the Fairy she would give him to her on the third day after the Fairy returned.

rows.question: Why couldn't the Old Woman take the son immediately?
answers: She had to follow the laws of Fairy-land.
By the laws of the Fairy-land
rows.said: Because the Old Woman is a Wicked Fairy who cannot take the bairn until the third day after the bargain.

rows.question: What did the widowed Mistress do after the Old woman disappeared?
answers: fell down in a dead faint beside the stone
Fall down in a dead faint beside the stone
rows.said: She sat in her kitchen crying and hugging her baby.

rows.question: What will the widowed Mistress do the next day?
answers: sit in her kitchen and cry, and hug her baby tighter in her arms
Nothing but sit in her kitchen and cry, and hug her baby
rows.said: She will sit in her kitchen and cry, hugging her baby tighter in her arms.

rows.question: Where did the widowed Mistress go during her walk?
answers: in the fir wood behind the house
The fir wood behind the house
rows.said: In the fir wood behind the house.

rows.question: What did the widowed Mistress hear while she went for a walk?
answers: the whirr of a spinning-wheel and the sound of a voice lilting a song
The whir of a spinning-wheel
rows.said: She heard a spinning-wheel whirring and a voice singing "Little kens our guid dame at hame, Whippety-Stourie is my name."

rows.question: How did the widowed Mistress feel after she heard a sound during her walk?
answers: surprised
Astonishment
rows.said: She felt astonished.

rows.question: Why did the widowed Mistress lay down her child at the tree root?
answers: She wanted to find where the sound came from.
To investigat the noise in the Quarry
rows.said: To hide from the Fairy who had taken her son.

rows.question: What did the widowed Mistress do after she laid down her son?
answers: crept noiselessly through the bushes on her hands and knees to the edge of the hole and peeped over
Creep noiselessly torugh the bushes on her hands and knees
rows.said: She sat in her kitchen and cried, hugging her baby tighter in her arms.

rows.question: Where did the widowed Mistress find the cruel Fairy?
answers: at the bottom of the quarry
At the bottom of the quarry
rows.said: In the fir wood behind the house of Kittlerumpit.

rows.question: What did the cruel Fairy do at the bottom of the quarry?
answers: spun away
Spinning away as fast as she could at a tiny spinning-wheel
rows.said: She spun a spinning-wheel and sang a song.

rows.question: How did the widowed Mistress find out the Old Woman's name?
answers: The Old Woman revealed her name in a song.
The fairy sang a song with her name in it
rows.said: She heard the Fairy singing "Whippety-Stourie is my name" while spinning at a spinning-wheel.

rows.question: What is the cruel Fairy's name?
answers: Whippety-Stourie
Whippety-Stourie
rows.said: Little kens our guid dame at hame, Whippety-Stourie is my name.

rows.question: Why did the widowed Mistress almost cry aloud for joy?
answers: She had learned the Fairy's secret, and her child was safe.
She had learned the fairy's secret
rows.said: She was relieved that her cherished pig had been cured by the Fairy.

rows.question: Why did the widowed Mistress crept softly back to the place where she had left her child?
answers: She was worried the Old Woman heard her.
In case the wicked old dame would hear her and throw some other spell over her
rows.said: To avoid the Fairy's spell that would have killed her.

rows.question: Why was the widowed Mistress singing, laughing, and tossing her child in the air?
answers: She found out the Old Woman's name.
She had learned the fairy's secret
rows.said: To celebrate the Fairy's promise to return for her child in three days.

rows.question: What did the widowed Mistress want to do before she let the Old Woman know about her name?
answers: tease the Fairy for a few minutes
Tease the fairy for a few minutes
rows.said: She intended to tease the Fairy for a few minutes before revealing her name.

rows.question: What did the widowed Mistress do after she saw the Old Woman coming up the hill?
answers: crumpled up her nice clean cap, and screwed up her face, and pretended to be in great distress and to be crying bitterly
Crumpled up her nice clean cap, and screwed up her face, and preteneded to be in great distress
rows.said: She cried out to the Old Woman to come to the house of Kittlerumpit.

rows.question: What did the widowed Mistress want to give to the Old Woman instead of her son?
answers: the pig
The pig
rows.said: The widow wanted to give the pig to the Old Woman instead of her son.

rows.question: Why didn't the Old woman want to take the pig?
answers: She did not eat bacon.
She had no need of bacon
rows.said: The Old woman did not want to take the pig because she believed the Fairy was a wicked witch who would harm her if she did.

rows.question: What did the widowed Mistress offer after the Old Woman declined the pig?
answers: herself
Take herself
rows.said: She offered her son.

rows.question: How did the Old Woman feel after the widowed Mistress offered herself?
answers: astonished
Astonishment
rows.said: She was astonished and delighted.

rows.question: Why didn't the Old Woman want to take the widowed Mistress?
answers: The widowed Mistress was not pretty.
She was a plain-looking, red-eyed, dowdy wife
rows.said: The Old Woman refused to take the widow's son because she was a wicked Fairy who could not take the child until the third day after the bargain.

rows.question: Why didn't the widowed Mistress tease the Old Woman anymore?
answers: The widowed Mistress became angry at her.
She got mad at the Old woman
rows.said: She was too late to pray for mercy, as the Fairy had already taken her son.

rows.question: What happened after the widowed Mistress revealed the Old Woman's name?
answers: She jumped into the air.
The Old Woman ran down the brae, shrieking with rage and disappointment
rows.said: The Fairy, Whippety-Stourie, chased the widow down the hill and she ran away screaming.
